1.title: What is the window peeper trend?
1.body: It's a staged comedy bit on TikTok. A camera creeps up to one lit window in a dark building at night. The person inside is eating, notices the camera, freezes, stares straight into the lens for too long, then pulls the curtain shut. The person in the window is the person who posts it.

2.title: Which photos can I use?
2.body: A photo of yourself, or of an adult who gave you permission. Don't upload photos of children or public figures. One person, waist up, facing the camera, in good light. JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to {size} MB.

3.title: How long is the video, and how long does it take?
3.body: About 12 seconds, with music. Making it usually takes a few minutes. Keep the page open, and the video plays there when it's ready.

4.title: How much does it cost?
4.body: A window peeper video costs {credits, plural, one {# credit} other {# credits}}. A Pro video, in sharper 1080p, costs {proCredits, plural, one {# credit} other {# credits}}. Credits come in one-time packs: {packs}. There is no subscription, and credits never expire. If a video fails, the credits are refunded. Every account also gets one free preview: 5 seconds with a watermark. See the <pricing>pricing page</pricing>.

5.title: Is the window peeper video free?
5.body: The preview is. Every account gets one free 5-second preview with a watermark, so you can see your photo in the scene before you pay. The full 12-second video without a watermark costs credits.

6.title: Do I need the CapCut template?
6.body: No. A CapCut window peeper template pastes your face into someone else's footage, inside the app. This site makes a new video of the person in your photo, in your own outfit, in your phone's or computer's browser. You only download the MP4.

7.title: Is there a window peeper filter on TikTok?
7.body: Not one that stages the whole scene. A camera filter changes the live picture; it can't film a night building, push in on a window and close a curtain. That's why people use templates or AI video for this trend. Here you upload a photo and get the finished clip.

8.title: Can I post it on TikTok, Reels or Shorts?
8.body: Yes. Every video from the home page is a vertical 9:16 MP4 that fills a phone screen. Post it with #windowpeeper, and add the trending sound in the app if you want it.

9.title: Does the video include sound?
9.body: Yes. Every video comes with original music made for it. It doesn't include the trend's sound. To use that, add it in TikTok, Reels or Shorts when you post, and lower the original audio there.

10.title: Do I need an account?
10.body: Yes, to make a video. Sign in with an email link or your Google account, no password needed. Your photo stays picked while you sign in.

11.title: Are my photos private?
11.body: Your photo is used only to make your video, and it is deleted about 24 hours after upload. We don't use photos or videos to train AI models. Your videos stay in your library, which only you can see, until you delete your account.

12.title: How do I contact support?
12.body: Email <email></email>. We reply within 3 business days.

about.title: About the window peeper AI video

text.1: This window peeper AI generator turns one photo into the trend's video. You upload a picture of one adult, and the AI films that person in a lit window at night: the camera creeps closer, they freeze mid-bite, stare into the lens and yank the curtain shut. The video is about 12 seconds long, vertical 9:16 or widescreen 16:9, with original music, and you download it as an MP4.
text.2: You don't film anything and you don't need editing skills. The <generator>generator at the top of this page</generator> does the whole job: pick a photo, choose Standard or Pro and press Generate. The <howto>step-by-step guide</howto> walks through it.

template.title: A new video, not a CapCut template

text.1: Most window peeper videos are made with a CapCut template: a finished edit with a slot for your face. The body, the table and the room belong to someone else's footage, which is why so many posts look alike.
text.2: This generator films a new scene around the person in your photo. Your face, hair and outfit move together, in your own clothes. That is also why the photo matters: one person, facing the camera, in good light, gives the best likeness.

trend.title: What the window peeper trend is

text.1: The window peeper trend is a short comedy bit. Seen from across the street, one window glows in a dark building. Inside, someone eats alone. They notice the camera, stop chewing and stare back far too long, then get up and close the curtain.
text.2: The joke is the stare. Nobody is really watching: the person in the window is the person who made the clip, and the video says so. Keep it that way, and make videos of yourself or of friends who are in on it.

text.1: People search for a window peeper filter or a window peeper effect, but a camera filter only changes the live picture. It can't stage a night building, push in on one window and close a curtain on cue.
text.2: The clips you see are either CapCut templates or AI videos like the ones made here. Upload a photo at the <back>generator</back> and you get the whole effect as one video file.

text.1: On TikTok the trend is usually posted with a trending sound. Every video made here comes with its own original music instead, so you can post it anywhere without borrowing someone else's track.
text.2: If you want the trending sound, add it in the app when you post. Most short-video apps let you lower or mute the original audio and pick a sound from their library.

social.title: Posting to TikTok, Reels and Shorts

text.1: Videos from the home page are 9:16, the shape of a phone screen, so they fill TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts with nothing cut off.
text.2: You can also send the MP4 straight to a group chat, or press Share under the video to open your phone's share menu.

how-to-make-window-peeper-video.title: How to make a window peeper video
how-to-make-window-peeper-video.tagline: One photo, six steps, one stare.
how-to-make-window-peeper-video.lead: You need one photo and a few minutes. This guide walks through each step on the generator, what it costs, and how to get a good result.

text.1: You need a photo, an email address or a Google account to sign in, and enough credits for one video, or your one free preview. Credit packs are one-time payments, not a subscription, and credits never expire.

1.title: Pick a photo
1.body: Open the <generator>generator on the home page</generator> and choose a photo of one adult, waist up, facing the camera, in good light. It must be a JPEG, PNG or WebP up to {size} MB, from {min, number} to {maxSide, number} pixels on each side.

2.title: Confirm it's OK to use
2.body: Pressing the button confirms the photo is yours, or that the adult in it agreed. A note under the button says so.

3.title: Choose Standard or Pro
3.body: Standard costs {credits} credits and is 720p. Pro costs {proCredits} credits and is 1080p. Both make the same scene, about 12 seconds long, with music. To see your photo in the scene first, try the free 5-second preview.

4.title: Sign in
4.body: Press Generate. If you aren't signed in, sign in with an email link or Google in the window that opens. Your photo stays picked while you do.

5.title: Pay if you need credits
5.body: If your balance is short, the generator offers the packs: {packs}. After checkout you come back to the page, and the video starts as soon as the credits arrive.

6.title: Wait, then download and post
6.body: A video usually takes a few minutes. Keep the page open, and it plays there when it's ready. Download saves the MP4. Post it to TikTok with #windowpeeper, and add the trending sound in the app if you want it.

list.1: One person only. The scene has one person at the table.
list.2: Waist up, facing the camera, with nothing covering the face.
list.3: Wear what you want in the video. The outfit comes from the photo.
list.4: Use even light. Dark or backlit photos give a blurry face.
list.5: Skip heavy filters, stickers and text on the photo.

text.1: If a video fails, or doesn't finish within 24 hours, its credits go back to your balance automatically. You don't need to contact us. If a photo is refused, try a different one; you don't lose credits for it.
text.2: If you leave the page, the video still finishes. It appears in your video library, and we email you when it's ready. For anything else, email <email></email>.

text.1: Your photo is used only to make your video, and it is deleted about 24 hours after upload. The finished video stays in your library until you delete your account. The <privacy>Privacy Policy</privacy> has the details.
text.2: Only upload photos of yourself, or of an adult who agreed. No photos of children or public figures, and nothing meant to deceive, harass or frighten anyone. The trend is a joke about being watched; keep it one.
